nodes.norm_label: d40 — qdrant over a numpy dot product — and not for speed

nodes.label: Cosine similarity — the angle, not a percentage
nodes.norm_label: cosine similarity — the angle, not a percentage
nodes.rationale: Ranking is by angle between vectors. The score is not a probability: two random chunks in this corpus score 0.540 on average, so a raw number is unreadable without that baseline.

nodes.label: Hybrid search / BM25 keyword retrieval (Phase 3)
nodes.rationale: The fix for rarity: table_names is 1.38% of the text it lives in and invisible to a dense embedder that averages tokens, while rarity is the strongest signal BM25's IDF has. Fixes three of four symbol misses and never the fourth, which is a ceiling.

nodes.label: Unit normalisation (every vector length exactly 1.0)
nodes.rationale: Buys the identity dot == cosine, so the cheap operation is the correct one rather than an approximation of it. Without it magnitude can beat relevance — an unrelated chunk scaled x3 wins on raw dot product. What it throws away is magnitude, which carried no ranking information here. Printing min and max is a check, not a statistic.

nodes.label: Version skew (future=True across 1.4 and 2.0)
nodes.rationale: 1.4's tutorial teaches future=True in 13 files; 2.0's has dropped it to 2. Dense retrieval returns a confident, correctly-sourced 1.4 passage and the answer is wrong. nodes.label: D02 — SQLAlchemy 1.4 → 2.0 as the subject
nodes.rationale: Three properties had to hold at once: the migration is finished so the answer set does not move; it mixes code, prose and error messages; and the failures are subtle rather than loud. Locked.

nodes.label: D03 — The corpus is measured, not scraped
nodes.norm_label: d03 — the corpus is measured, not scraped

nodes.label: D05 — Zero paid API calls
nodes.rationale: Cost control, and more importantly a paid API hides the parts worth learning — VRAM budgeting, batch sizes, why model choice is a trade. Accepted cost: local models give worse answers than a GPT-4 version. Locked.

nodes.label: D11 — corpus/raw/ is fetched, never committed
nodes.norm_label: d11 — corpus/raw/ is fetched, never committed

nodes.label: D12 — The manifest carries no timestamp
nodes.norm_label: d12 — the manifest carries no timestamp
nodes.rationale: A timestamp makes every rebuild produce a diff even when nothing changed, and a diff that is always present is a diff nobody reads. Without it the manifest is a pure function of the two tags and the selection rules.

nodes.label: D14 — The measurement rule
nodes.rationale: Every time it was violated here the underlying claim turned out to be wrong or unreproducible — a state trace with no file behind it, a hardcoded issue_id in (1,3), a wrong flush/commit answer, a fabricated table. The most transferable thing in the project. Locked.

nodes.label: D15 — The example rule
nodes.rationale: Prose hides errors that examples expose: 03-PRACTICE-APP.md described a schema for 292 lines with no code block and asserted 'six tables' — there are six mapped classes and eight tables.

nodes.label: D16 — Pin image tags rather than using latest
nodes.norm_label: d16 — pin image tags rather than using latest
nodes.rationale: latest means whatever was newest at pull time, so two machines can silently run different majors; Postgres majors are not on-disk compatible.

nodes.label: D17 — Test real 2.0 without upgrading the project
nodes.norm_label: d17 — test real 2.0 without upgrading the project

nodes.label: D18 — python:3.11-slim, not Alpine

'Smallest base image' is a bad default; the right question is which libc the wheels target.

nodes.label: D19 — The image holds code; the container holds data
nodes.norm_label: d19 — the image holds code; the container holds data
nodes.rationale: A build-time seed produces a fixture, not a database: it lands in a read-only layer so every write goes to the container's writable layer and disappears. The failure is silent. Once Postgres has its own container the wrong option stops being expressible. Locked.

nodes.label: D20 — image: is declared explicitly in Compose
nodes.norm_label: d20 — image: is declared explicitly in compose
nodes.rationale: With build: and no image:, Compose invents a name from project and service — a different image from anything tagged by hand, both current, drifting apart in silence. A stale image 13 hours older than the code once invalidated a networking measurement.

nodes.label: D21 — Service-name DNS, no published ports
nodes.norm_label: d21 — service-name dns, no published ports
nodes.rationale: localhost inside a container means that container. Publishing a port is for host access and the app is not on the host. --network also provides isolation: a container on the default bridge cannot reach a user-defined network even by IP.

nodes.label: D22 — Healthcheck plus condition: service_healthy
nodes.rationale: depends_on alone waits for the container to start, not for Postgres to accept connections — the gap is where the flaky-on-CI-only bug lives. A sleep is a guess that is simultaneously too long and occasionally too short.

nodes.label: D24 — Tests pin what the docs claim, not what SQLAlchemy does
nodes.norm_label: d24 — tests pin what the docs claim, not what sqlalchemy does
nodes.rationale: The failure mode this project actually has is documentation drifting from reality, and prose has no test. Testing that SQLAlchemy works is SQLAlchemy's job.

nodes.label: D25 — Every test is mutation-checked
nodes.rationale: A test that cannot fail is decoration. Two corpus tests were checked by breaking what they describe; a sed that silently did not match during one of those checks is exactly why the check is run rather than assumed.

nodes.label: D26 — The CI gate was proved with a deliberately failing PR
nodes.norm_label: d26 — the ci gate was proved with a deliberately failing pr
nodes.rationale: 'I set up CI' and 'I proved CI blocks a bad merge' are different claims and only the second survives 'how do you know?'. Corrected 2026-08-16: the docs reproduce job existed in ci.yml but was never a required context, so the rule the repo cares most about was enforced by a job nobody had to pass. On its first enforced run it caught a NumPy ModuleNotFoundError that passed locally.

nodes.label: D27 — Device is a flag, not an assumption (--device mps/cuda/cpu)
nodes.norm_label: d27 — device is a flag, not an assumption (--device mps/cuda/cpu)
nodes.rationale: The lab PC is shared and went away for two days; a plan whose only answer is 'wait' has a single point of failure that is somebody else's calendar.

nodes.label: D28 — Langfuse stays in Phase 6
nodes.rationale: There is nothing to observe yet and a second Postgres + ClickHouse + Redis + MinIO + web pile is ops noise during Phases 0–5. Explicitly NOT a RAM constraint — 31 GiB would fit it, and the RAM justification died when the hardware was measured.

nodes.label: D29 — Handoff to the lab PC goes through git, not chat
nodes.norm_label: d29 — handoff to the lab pc goes through git, not chat
nodes.rationale: The Mac and the lab PC cannot route to each other — ssh reports 'Operation timed out', the signature of no route — so commands typed into chat bounce back unrun. A git branch is an asynchronous wire that works with no network path at all.

nodes.label: D32 — Embedding model comparison is between models, not machines
nodes.norm_label: d32 — embedding model comparison is between models, not machines

nodes.label: D36 — Embedding writes a file; loading into Qdrant is separate
nodes.norm_label: d36 — embedding writes a file; loading into qdrant is separate
nodes.rationale: A file makes the index an input rather than a side effect: copyable, loadable anywhere, resumable after a failure, and never the only copy.

nodes.label: D37 — Pin the embedding model revision, not just its name
nodes.norm_label: d37 — pin the embedding model revision, not just its name
nodes.rationale: 'BGE-M3' is not reproducible; vectors from two revisions are not comparable at all — cosine between them is noise, not degradation.

nodes.label: D41 — Collection name carries model and revision
nodes.norm_label: d41 — collection name carries model and revision
nodes.rationale: Qdrant has no collection-level metadata field, so the fact goes in the name — re-embedding with a different revision produces a different collection rather than a silently mixed one.

nodes.label: D42 — Qdrant publishes one port, bound to 127.0.0.1
nodes.norm_label: d42 — qdrant publishes one port, bound to 127.0.0.1
nodes.rationale: Its client rag/index.py runs on the host, so the host genuinely is outside; the short form 6333:6333 would bind 0.0.0.0 and expose an unauthenticated vector database to every network the laptop joins.

nodes.label: D48 — The 3060 embeds 2.8x faster than the M4
nodes.norm_label: d48 — the 3060 embeds 2.8x faster than the m4
nodes.rationale: 19.9 vs 7.2 chunks/s, closing D27's untested half.

nodes.label: D49 — Bigger batches are slower on CUDA too
nodes.norm_label: d49 — bigger batches are slower on cuda too
nodes.rationale: Batch 8 beats 128 by 2.7x at an eighth of the VRAM; variable-length chunks make batching pad rather than amortise.

nodes.label: Refusal clause A — 'say exactly: the sources do not answer this'
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause a — 'say exactly: the sources do not answer this'
nodes.rationale: Hands the model a canned sentence it may emit instead of answering; 'do not contain the answer' is a high bar and it over-fires, refusing a question whose answer is present.

nodes.label: Refusal clause B — prefer answering, refuse only if the sources are silent
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause b — prefer answering, refuse only if the sources are silent
nodes.rationale: What shipped after Step 4. Same canned sentence as a last resort rather than the default exit. Later shown by Round 8 to refuse the same 8 questions as A, identically.

nodes.label: Refusal clause C — no refusal instruction at all
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause c — no refusal instruction at all
nodes.rationale: Proves the clause is necessary: it invented a complete method signature for Session.execute out of the model's weights, exactly the hallucination D07 predicted.

nodes.label: Refusal clause D — partial answers expected, refusal narrowed to subject
nodes.norm_label: refusal clause d — partial answers expected, refusal narrowed to subject
nodes.rationale: A genuinely different fourth wording rather than a tuning of B: it makes partial answers the expected output, narrows refusal to subject rather than sufficiency, and requires a refusal to name what was looked for. Confirmed at n=5 with zero non-unanimous cells; its margin over B is Q16 at 5/5 against 0/5.

nodes.label: build_prompt() — this question's pages plus the question
nodes.norm_label: build_prompt() — this question's pages plus the question
nodes.rationale: The pile that does change: the five retrieved chunks rendered as numbered SOURCES followed by QUESTION and ANSWER. --show-prompt prints both piles.

nodes.label: The engine.execute refusal — the named bug
nodes.norm_label: the engine.execute refusal — the named bug
nodes.rationale: The five pages handed to the model already contained the answer and the reply was 'The sources do not answer this'. Proved to be the instruction rather than search by handing the model only the on-topic chunks, which it also refused.

nodes.label: Prompt A — strict canned refusal
nodes.rationale: Tells the model to emit a fixed sentence if the sources do not contain the answer. Over-fired once in 13 runs and never reproduced; refuses the same 8 of 19 questions as B, identically.

nodes.label: Prompt B — refusal as last resort (shipped, then replaced)
nodes.norm_label: prompt b — refusal as last resort (shipped, then replaced)
nodes.rationale: Prefer answering from what the sources do say; refuse only if they are genuinely silent. Correct in 26 of 26 cells on two questions, but wrong in 5 of 19 over the full probe set, and behaviourally identical to A.

nodes.label: Prompt C — no refusal instruction
nodes.rationale: The control. Answers all 19 questions including the three the corpus provably cannot answer, and fabricates a Session.execute signature 13 times out of 13 — stable rather than random, same four arguments each time. Proves the failure is in the instruction, not the model.

nodes.label: Prompt D — partial answers expected, refusal narrowed to subject (shipped)
nodes.norm_label: prompt d — partial answers expected, refusal narrowed to subject (shipped)
nodes.rationale: Makes partial answers the expected output, narrows refusal to subject rather than sufficiency, and requires a refusal to name what was looked for. Fixes B's under-fire on Q16 (5/5 against B's 0/5) and makes zero prompt errors at k=5.

nodes.label: qwen2.5-coder:7b via Ollama
nodes.rationale: The generator. 62.23 tok/s warm on the RTX 3060 against 18.4 on the M4. Nothing is trained — the model is fixed and only the prompt changes.

nodes.label: §R3 — The instructions are a component, like the search
nodes.norm_label: §r3 — the instructions are a component, like the search
nodes.rationale: The prompt is a component that can be wrong on its own: search returned the right pages and one standing sentence threw them away unread.

nodes.label: The refusal clause ('The sources do not answer this')
nodes.norm_label: the refusal clause ('the sources do not answer this')
nodes.rationale: Simultaneously load-bearing and harmful: without it the model invents API signatures every time, with it phrased strictly it can refuse a question whose answer is in the prompt. Necessity is the strong claim; over-firing is the weak one.

nodes.label: SYSTEM — the standing rules (system prompt)
nodes.rationale: The pile of text that does not change between questions. The bug in this sitting lives in it: search returned the right pages and one standing sentence threw them away unread.

nodes.label: Round 1 — sshd and the LAN address
nodes.norm_label: round 1 — sshd and the lan address
nodes.rationale: CLOSED 2026-08-13: sshd enabled and active, user shaili, key installed.

nodes.label: Round 10 — the run that separates the prompt from retrieval
nodes.norm_label: round 10 — the run that separates the prompt from retrieval
nodes.rationale: 152 generations at k=5 and k=10. Q18 and Q19 have their chunks in the prompt at k=10 and every wording still refuses; Q5 was fabricated at k=10 by A, B and D.

nodes.label: Round 11 — run it to a conclusion, not to another round
nodes.norm_label: round 11 — run it to a conclusion, not to another round
nodes.rationale: 380 generations, k=5, repeat=5. Zero non-unanimous cells — every cell 0/5 or 5/5 — so refusal behaviour is deterministic here and Q16 is D=5 B=0 on all five runs.

nodes.label: Round 2 — the LAN is not a route, so Tailscale is the only way in
nodes.norm_label: round 2 — the lan is not a route, so tailscale is the only way in
nodes.rationale: Measured from the Mac: the LAN address does not route, so Tailscale is the only inbound path.

nodes.label: Round 6 — settle D43's A cell, which the Mac cannot
nodes.norm_label: round 6 — settle d43's a cell, which the mac cannot
nodes.rationale: Ten runs: prompt A refused the answerable question 0/10 on this box, so the over-fire never reproduced; B was correct in every cell; C always answered the unanswerable question.

nodes.label: Round 7 — does raising k fix failures Phase 3 was going to fix?
nodes.norm_label: round 7 — does raising k fix failures phase 3 was going to fix?
nodes.rationale: refused stayed 8 at k=5, 6 and 10 while retrieval_failure fell 5 to 4 to 3. The backref chunk is in the prompt at k=10 and the model still refused, so the eight refusals are not the argument for hybrid search.

nodes.label: Round 8 — is the refusal clause the reason, or the model?
nodes.norm_label: round 8 — is the refusal clause the reason, or the model?
nodes.rationale: A and B refuse the same 8 questions identically, so D43 chose between two options that are the same option. C refuses 0 and fabricates. The correct floor is 5.

nodes.label: Round 9 — a fourth wording, and the first one that is a different mechanism
nodes.norm_label: round 9 — a fourth wording, and the first one that is a different mechanism
nodes.rationale: D refused 9: the right five plus the same four over-fires as B, and Q16 which A and B answered.

nodes.label: HANDOFF.md — the Mac to lab-PC wire
nodes.norm_label: handoff.md — the mac to lab-pc wire
nodes.rationale: Claude runs on the Mac and cannot reach the lab PC, which has no inbound route until sshd and a tunnel exist. Claude writes ASK blocks; Viraj runs them and pastes raw output into REPLY blocks.

nodes.label: Generation — study notes (§R3)
nodes.rationale: Split out of 10-RETRIEVAL because generation is a genuinely different subject from retrieval; numbering continued rather than restarted (D47).

nodes.label: The healthcheck that lied (/dev/tcp under CMD-SHELL)
nodes.norm_label: the healthcheck that lied (/dev/tcp under cmd-shell)
nodes.rationale: CMD-SHELL runs the string through /bin/sh, which is dash on this image, and /dev/tcp is a bash builtin rather than a real device. The container served traffic perfectly and reported unhealthy forever — the worst failure shape available, because anything using condition: service_healthy would wait forever on a service that was ready.

nodes.label: The bug that ate an afternoon — it was the prompt
nodes.norm_label: the bug that ate an afternoon — it was the prompt
nodes.rationale: The first run refused a question whose answer was in the prompt. Two hypotheses were tested and ruled out by experiment (cross-version duplicates eating slots; retrieval ranking it too low) before the system prompt was found. The prompt is the one component nobody suspects because it is hand-written rather than measured.

nodes.label: D43 — The refusal clause is necessary and over-fires
nodes.norm_label: d43 — the refusal clause is necessary and over-fires
nodes.rationale: C invents API signatures without it; A refused a question whose answer was in the prompt. Measured at 1 refusal in 13 — later shown by D52 to have chosen between two options that were the same option.

nodes.label: D44 — Fixing the prompt was correct, not tuning
nodes.norm_label: d44 — fixing the prompt was correct, not tuning
nodes.rationale: D04 withholds hybrid search and reranking; it does not license shipping a component that does not work. Simple and broken are different.

nodes.label: D51 — Refusals are not a retrieval problem
nodes.norm_label: d51 — refusals are not a retrieval problem
nodes.rationale: Sweeping k moved retrieval and left refused at 8 at every value — later corrected in place by D54, which found the Rounds 8-9 runs were at k=5 where the answers were not retrieved.

nodes.label: D52 — A genuinely different fourth prompt wording
nodes.norm_label: d52 — a genuinely different fourth prompt wording
nodes.rationale: Round 8 showed A and B refuse the same 8 questions identically, so D43 chose between two options that are the same option; D makes partial answers expected and narrows refusal to subject rather than sufficiency.

nodes.label: D54 — Ship prompt D, keep DEFAULT_K = 5
nodes.norm_label: d54 — ship prompt d, keep default_k = 5
nodes.rationale: D at k=5 is the only configuration measured with zero prompt errors; k=10 trades four honest refusals for two over-fires and one fabrication. Corrects D51 in place: at k=5 the failures ARE retrieval failures.
